title: One smooth skin
goals: How the industry makes a body's skin, researched and written down
The Body's skin one closed surface: a cage wrapped on our anatomy, made smooth
Bound to the rig: five poses without a tear
Lit as skin is: light under it, two lobes of gloss, tone place by place
Seen in the library on a real GPU, and timed
Photoreal: a truer form, a face, hair

clips.name: The meadow, one tent

clips.name: Towards the tent

clips.name: Back and up

captions.text: One skin where there were seven pieces
Currently the naked skin body looks still not photorealistic!
We need to upgrade the architecture to latest industry best practices
to make the human body really photorealistic and smooth.
A film's body is one cage of four-sided faces, made smooth.
Ours was drawn out of voxels: seven pieces, 1 410 open edges.
Now it is one closed skin, wrapped on our own anatomy.
Its thighs met to the knees. Now they stand apart.
Lit as skin is: red light spreads a millimetre under it.
It bends at elbow, knee and shoulder without a tear.
Smooth, yes. Photoreal, not yet: the form, the face, the hair.
Seen on a software GPU only. Not yet in the library.
